q01.key_idea: Match the stickers by size and shape: 2 small circles, 2 long black ovals and 2 big circles.
steps: The stickers are drawn in gray, so look at their size and shape, not their color.
There are 2 small circles, 2 long black ovals and 2 big circles. That is 6 stickers.
Butterfly A has 2 big circles on its top wings and 2 small circles on its bottom wings.
Each small circle has a long black oval on it. That uses all 6 stickers, and nothing else.

choice_feedback.B: The black spots here are little round dots, but the stickers have long ovals, not dots.
choice_feedback.C: The black spots on the top wings are round dots. There are no round dot stickers.
choice_feedback.D: This butterfly needs 4 small circles, but there are only 2.
choice_feedback.E: The black spots here are round dots, and there are no long black ovals at all.

q02.key_idea: Each cut makes one more piece, so count where the dashed line crosses the string and add 1.
steps: Start at the scissors and slide your finger along the dashed line.
Make a mark every time the line crosses the string: through the big round loop, through the small curl inside it, and then up across the wavy part.
At the top right the string makes a little hook, and the crossings are very close together. Go slowly there so you do not miss one.
The line crosses the string 8 times. 8 cuts make 8 + 1 = 9 pieces.

choice_feedback.A: That is too few. Count every place where the dashed line crosses the string.
choice_feedback.B: That is too few. Some crossings are close together, so check the curl and the top right hook again.
choice_feedback.C: That is too few. Look again at the top right, where the crossings are close together.
choice_feedback.D: 8 is the number of cuts. Each cut makes one more piece, so there is 1 more piece than cuts.

q03.key_idea: Count the missing blocks row by row, using the blocks next to the hole as a ruler.
steps: Look at the rows that have a hole in them. Use the blocks next to the hole to see how many would fit.
In the third row from the top, 2 blocks are missing. In the fourth row, 3 blocks are missing.
In the fifth row, 4 blocks are missing. In the sixth row, just 1 block is missing.

choice_feedback.A: That is too few. Count row by row: 2, 3, 4 and 1.
choice_feedback.B: That is 1 too few. Do not forget the single block missing in the lowest row of the hole.
choice_feedback.D: That is 1 too many. Count row by row: 2 + 3 + 4 + 1 = 10.
choice_feedback.E: That is too many. Count row by row: 2 + 3 + 4 + 1 = 10.

q04.key_idea: Follow the string from pearl to pearl to find the order of the colors.
steps: Start at the black pearl at the top and follow the string.
It goes to a white pearl, then down to the black pearl at the bottom, then to the other white pearl, and back to the top.
So going around, the pearls are black, white, black, white. The colors take turns.
In band E, the pearls go white, black, white, black. The colors take turns, so it is the same bracelet.

choice_feedback.A: Here the 2 black pearls are next to each other over the top of the band. In the bracelet a black pearl always sits between 2 white ones.
choice_feedback.B: Here 2 black pearls sit side by side. In the bracelet the colors take turns.
choice_feedback.C: Here 2 black pearls sit side by side. In the bracelet the colors take turns.
choice_feedback.D: Here 2 black pearls sit side by side. In the bracelet the colors take turns.

q05.key_idea: Try leaving out each number and see if the other 4 can be split into 2 pairs with the same sum.
steps: The two sides must be equal, so we need 2 pairs of numbers with the same total.
Leave out 4. The numbers left are 1, 3, 5 and 7.
1 + 7 = 8 and 3 + 5 = 8. Both sides are 8!
So 4 is the number that was not used.

choice_feedback.A: Without 1 we have 3, 4, 5, 7. No way to split them gives 2 equal sums.
choice_feedback.B: Without 3 we have 1, 4, 5, 7. No way to split them gives 2 equal sums.
choice_feedback.D: Without 5 we have 1, 3, 4, 7. No way to split them gives 2 equal sums.
choice_feedback.E: Without 7 we have 1, 3, 4, 5. No way to split them gives 2 equal sums.

q06.key_idea: Jim moves around the wheel the same number of seats, in the same direction, as Ben.
steps: The wheel has 6 seats. Ben is at the top. Jim is in the lower left seat.
Ben moves to Jim's seat. Going to the left, that is 2 seats: top, then upper left, then lower left.
Jim moves 2 seats the same way: from lower left to the bottom, then to the lower right.
So Jim is now in the lower right seat.

choice_feedback.A: The top seat is where Ben was before. Jim does not end up there.
choice_feedback.B: Jim moves 2 seats the same way Ben did. He ends up in the lower right seat, not the upper right one.
choice_feedback.D: That is the wrong way. Ben moved down the left side, so Jim moves down too, toward the bottom.
choice_feedback.E: Jim moves 2 seats, not just 1. The bottom seat is only 1 seat away.

q07.key_idea: After 4 turns the block looks just like it did at the start, so the pictures repeat.
steps: In the answers, the light gray squares are colored blue and the dark gray squares are colored orange. Match them by where they are.
After 4 turns the block is back where it started. So after 8 turns it is back at the start too.
Turns 9 and 10 are just like turns 1 and 2. So the block looks like the picture after turn 2.
After turn 2 the block has 2 light squares at the top right and 2 dark squares at the bottom left. In D, the 2 blue squares are at the top right and the 2 orange squares are at the bottom left.

choice_feedback.A: The colored squares are in different places than in the picture after turn 2.
choice_feedback.B: This is how the block looked at the start, before any turns. That is after 8 turns, not 10.
choice_feedback.C: This is the picture after turn 1. After 10 turns the block looks like the picture after turn 2.
choice_feedback.E: Here the orange squares are at the top. After turn 2 the dark squares are at the bottom left.

q08.key_idea: Count the triangles first. Circles must be half of that, and squares double that.
steps: Count the shapes in each picture.
Picture E has 2 triangles, 1 circle and 4 squares.
1 circle is half of 2 triangles. 4 squares is twice 2 triangles, because 2 + 2 = 4.
Both rules work for E.

choice_feedback.A: A has 4 triangles but only 2 squares. There should be twice as many squares as triangles.
choice_feedback.B: B has 2 triangles and 4 circles. There should be fewer circles than triangles.
choice_feedback.C: C has 4 triangles, so it needs 8 squares, but it has only 5.
choice_feedback.D: D has 3 triangles, so it would need 6 squares, but it has 5.

q09.key_idea: Find the places of Leo and Max in the line.
steps: There are 7 people in front of Leo, so Leo is number 8 in the line.
Max stands right behind Leo, so Max is number 9.
There are 11 people in all. 11 - 9 = 2 people are behind Max.

choice_feedback.A: Max is number 9 of 11, so there are 2 people behind him, not 1.
choice_feedback.C: 3 people are behind Leo. Max stands behind Leo, so 1 fewer are behind Max.
choice_feedback.D: Max is number 9 of 11, so only 2 people are behind him.
choice_feedback.E: Max is number 9 of 11, so only 2 people are behind him.

q10.key_idea: Half are cows when there are as many cows as other animals.
steps: The animals that are not cows are 1 horse and 3 pigs. 1 + 3 = 4.
For half to be cows, there must be 4 cows too.
He has 2 cows. 4 - 2 = 2 more cows.
Check: 4 cows and 4 other animals make 8 animals, and half of 8 is 4.

choice_feedback.A: He has 2 cows and 4 other animals. That is not half yet.
choice_feedback.B: With 1 more cow he has 3 cows and 4 other animals. That is not half.
choice_feedback.D: With 3 more cows he has 5 cows and 4 other animals. That is more than half.
choice_feedback.E: With 4 more cows he has 6 cows and 4 other animals. That is more than half.

q11.key_idea: Use the box with 14 to find the missing number on the left.
steps: The bottom row starts with ? on the left. Its first box is under 10 and shows 14.
The star is in the bottom row under 7. So it is 4 + 7 = 11.

choice_feedback.A: The star is 4 + 7. That is 11, not 10.
choice_feedback.C: 12 is 5 + 7, the box above the star. The star is 4 + 7.
choice_feedback.D: The star is 4 + 7. That is 11, not 13.
choice_feedback.E: The star is 4 + 7. That is 11, not 15.

q12.key_idea: First count the bars, then the dots, and pick the cheapest mix of sheets.
steps: Each crown needs 1 bar, 4 dots and 1 cross. 7 crowns need 7 bars, 28 dots and 7 crosses.
Only the first kind of sheet has bars, 2 on each. 3 sheets give just 6 bars, so she needs 4 of them. They also give 4 dots and 4 crosses.
She still needs 28 - 4 = 24 dots. The second kind of sheet has 5 dots. 4 sheets give only 20, so she needs 5 of them (25 dots).
That is plenty of crosses too. 4 + 5 = 9 sheets.

choice_feedback.A: 7 sheets cannot give enough bars and dots together. She needs 4 sheets for the bars and 5 more for the dots.
choice_feedback.C: She can do it with 4 sheets of the first kind and 5 of the second kind. That is only 9.
choice_feedback.D: She can do it with fewer: 4 sheets of the first kind and 5 of the second kind make 9.
choice_feedback.E: She can do it with fewer: 4 sheets of the first kind and 5 of the second kind make 9.

q13.key_idea: The tiles can be turned but not flipped over, because the back is white.
steps: Each tile is a zigzag of 4 squares with exactly 1 black square in the middle of the zigzag.
Simon can turn a tile, but he cannot flip it over. Then it would show the white back.
In pattern A, lay the 2 tiles side by side, both turned like the second picture: 2 squares on top with the black one on the left, and 2 squares below, shifted to the left.
The 2 tiles fit next to each other and make pattern A.

choice_feedback.B: One of the tiles would have to be a mirror image, so Simon would need to flip it. Then its back would be white.
choice_feedback.C: This pattern has 3 black squares and 9 squares in all. 2 tiles have only 2 black squares and 8 squares.
choice_feedback.D: 2 zigzag tiles cannot fill this straight box. A corner is always left over.
choice_feedback.E: Both pieces here are mirror images of the tile, so Simon would have to flip them over.

q14.key_idea: After every 10 jumps there is a 3 minute break, but no break after the last jumps.
steps: 50 jumps is 5 lots of 10 jumps. Each lot takes 1 minute, so that is 5 minutes of jumping.
There is a break between the lots: after lot 1, 2, 3 and 4. That is 4 breaks.
4 breaks of 3 minutes is 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 minutes.
5 + 12 = 17 minutes.

choice_feedback.A: 4 is the number of breaks, not the number of minutes.
choice_feedback.B: 5 minutes is only the jumping time. The breaks take time too.
choice_feedback.C: Add the jumping and the breaks again: 5 + 12 = 17.
choice_feedback.E: The kangaroo is done after the last jumps. It does not need breaks after that.

q15.key_idea: ADA starts and ends with the same digit, so it must be a key like 141 or 717.
steps: ADA has the same first and last letter. Only the keys 141 and 717 start and end with the same digit.
If ADA were 717, then D would be 1, and DGA would start with 1. No other key starts with 1. So ADA is 141: A is 1 and D is 4.
DGA is 4, then G, then 1. That is 471, so G is 7. DAG is 4, 1, 7, which is 417.
The key left over is 717. 7 is G and 1 is A, so the letters are G, A, G.

choice_feedback.A: GDA would be 741, and there is no key 741.
choice_feedback.B: ADG would be 147, and there is no key 147.
choice_feedback.C: GAD would be 714, and there is no key 714.
choice_feedback.E: DAD would be 414, and there is no key 414.
